jobs.description:
As the leading company in the field of software solutions for healthcare, we operate in 19 countries and employ over 9,000 dedicated staff members. You will work in a dynamic and innovative environment full of opportunities. With your commitment and passion, you have the chance to make a sustainable difference.

CGM Leverages AI: We’re looking for people who feel the power of AI in the e-health environment, who want to help shape change, and who are driven by a curious passion to see how technology can make healthcare smarter, simpler, and better.

Together, we are shaping the healthcare system of the future. Become part of our mission and make a difference - for a world where knowledge saves lives!

Are you passionate about groundbreaking products? Do you have the talent to turn ideas into real, valuable solutions-while always keeping the bigger picture in mind? Then we’d love to meet you!

You define and drive the technology strategy together with the CTO and establish effective governance frameworks across on-premise, cloud, and hybrid environments. You set the architectural guardrails for AI-native development, ensuring that AI-generated code is consistently reviewed against our architectural principles.

You own technology lifecycle management-from introducing new capabilities through to modernizing and retiring existing systems.

You define the role of architecture within the FIRE team delivery model and establish it as a fixed, operational part of our product development.

You build the Architecture Guild as an active community of practice, develop Guild leaders within the teams, and coach architects and senior engineers.

Several years of experience as a senior architect or Head of architecture in a complex, enterprise-wide technology environment-with demonstrable hands-on delivery, not just strategic advisory.

Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture frameworks (e.g. TOGAF, Zachman) and domain-driven design in large-scale engineering contexts.

Practical experience with microservices, cloud-native, and event-driven architectures, ideally across both greenfield and modernization projects.

Familiarity with AI-native development models and the architectural implications of AI-generated code and autonomous agents.

Strong communication and stakeholder management skills - credible from engineering teams up to executive board level, ideally with experience in healthcare IT or another regulated industry.

Fluent in German and English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Mobile work: Work flexibly on the move two days a week and on site three days a week.

Attractive locations: In addition to fully equipped workplaces, regular events such as summer parties and Christmas parties await you at our locations.

Development: Our in-house academy and our portfolio of external cooperation partners will support you in your further development.

Health: Health is a valuable asset for us. Our in-house canteen offers a selection of tasty and healthy dishes every day, and we welcome you to our fully equipped fitness center for weekly courses (online & offline).

More is always possible: The kindergarten on our CGM campus in Koblenz helps our employees to organize their working day even more flexibly. We also offer corporate benefits, the option of a job bike, a company pension scheme, and much more.

You will work in a highly specialized team with direct customer contact, international project assignments, and a short path from idea to implementation.

Hardware design including component selection, schematic capture, and design for manufacturability (DFM/DFT)
Develop and integrate firmware (embedded C/C++) for microcontroller-based measurement and control systems
Systematically test, debug, and commission electronic assemblies directly in the lab - hands-on and solution-oriented

Strong ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and drive independent work.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and in German.

Experience with microfluidic systems, lab-on-chip, or MEMS

Experience with ISO 13485 / IEC 60601 or comparable regulatory frameworks

Real impact: You'll help shape our product architecture directly - your designs go into market-relevant life science devices and directly influence our customers' strategies.

Variety, not routine: Projects spanning multiple customers, applications (diagnostics, single-cell analysis, sequencing, lab automation), and development phases - no two days alike.

Top-tier team: Work alongside internationally experienced founders, AI engineers, and systems engineers.

Growth & responsibility: A clear development path in a fast-growing company - help shape our processes, methods, and team.

Flexibility & culture: Flexible working hours, short decision-making paths, and a collaborative culture (innovation, excellence, collaboration)

Attractive package: Competitive compensation and a modern workplace in the heart of Münster.

About betatron bio°
At betatron bio°, we believe that great engineering happens when deep technical expertise meets speed, curiosity, and practical execution.

We combine deep microfluidics expertise with systems engineering excellence and AI-powered development tools - for results that speak for themselves.

If you want to work on real-world engineering problems with real-world impact, rather than maintaining an established product for years, we would like to hear from you.

Research Associate / Project Coordinator (m/f/d)

The Department of Health Services Research at the Institute of Diversity Medicine, Faculty of Medicine, Ruhr University Bochum, Germany, is seeking to appoint a Research Associate / Project Coordinator (m/f/d) starting 1st of January 2027. The Department of Health Services Research investigates how individual diversity characteristics influence healthcare delivery and develops, implements, and evaluates innovative, patient-centred models of care. Our research focuses on the evaluation of complex interventions, participatory health services research, and the development of diversity-sensitive healthcare concepts. Our interdisciplinary work integrates health services research, public health, social sciences, and medical ethics.

The successful candidate will join the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's Programme DIME – Diversity Medicine, an international initiative to establish a new joint Master's programme together with leading European and international partner universities (e.g. France, Japan, Taiwan). This position offers the unique opportunity to contribute to the development of an innovative international degree programme at the intersection of diversity medicine, global health, and higher education. As Research Associate / Project Coordinator, you will play a central role in coordinating this international consortium. You will collaborate closely with academic partners, university leadership, teaching staff, students, and funding organisations across several countries. The position requires excellent English proficiency, strong interpersonal and diplomatic skills, and outstanding organisational abilities to successfully coordinate complex international collaborations.

Research associate (m/f/x) in Data Science in Chemistry

At the Chair of Inorganic Chemistry II of the Ruhr University Bochum we address research questions in the fields of organometallic synthesis chemistry and homogeneous catalysis. We are an internationally oriented research team that develops new reagents as well as highly efficient catalysts for synthetic chemistry. By combining advanced synthetic methods, state of the art analytical techniques, quantum chemical calculations, and machine learning methods, we conduct world leading research at the highest international level. Automated analysis of chemical data and the prediction of reactivity, selectivity and yield by means of machine learning are revolutionising modern chemistry. In our group we employ data science methods together with quantum chemical calculations to model reaction networks from experimental data, understand bonding situations and reactivities, and identify new catalysts and reaction conditions in a data driven way.

The Chair of Inorganic Chemistry II (Organometallic Chemistry and Homogeneous Catalysis) is looking for a full time scientific staff member (postdoctoral researcher) (100 % TV L 13) to start immediately. We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher (m/f/x) who, with a passion for interdisciplinary work, will support the design of teaching courses in data science and machine learning and strengthen our group in this area.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 2 Jahre
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-09-21

Your tasks:

- Quantum‑chemical calculations – perform calculations to elucidate reaction mechanisms, bonding situations and to extract physicochemical properties of molecules
- Model development & validation – create and validate models that clarify structure‑activity relationships and predict properties and reactivities; analyse data with statistical methods and visualise the results
- Collaboration with experimentalists – work closely with laboratory scientists to support and validate data collection
- Project leadership – take responsibility for projects, supervise students, write reports and grant proposals
- Scientific communication – compile results into publications and assist students in preparing manuscripts
- Mentorship – supervise students in their theses and support teaching activities in the areas of Data Science and Machine Learning
- Teaching – support the development and implementation of new student courses in Data Science and Machine Learning

Your profile:

A candidate with a completed university degree and a PhD (preferred) in Chemistry is sought; candidates from related fields such as Data Science or Computer Science with demonstrable knowledge of chemistry are also welcome.

Further requirements:

- Practical experience in quantum‑chemical calculations – familiarity with common quantum‑chemical programs and methods, in particular ORCA, Multiwfn, AIM, etc.
- Practical experience in machine learning & chemistry‑specific data science – programming skills in Python and hands‑on experience with standard libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Scikit‑learn, RDKit, PyTorch, etc.
- Practical experience in homogeneous catalysis – desirable, but not mandatory
- Practical experience with the installation and maintenance of high-performance computing clusters – desirable, but not mandatory
- Theoretical knowledge in quantum-chemistry, machine learning, molecular chemistry
- Experience in research project management
- Experience in publishing and presenting scientific results
- Experience in teaching and the supervision of students and interns
- Language skills – English (fluent spoken and written) is required; German is an advantage but not mandatory

Furthermore, the applicant should be open to team‑oriented work and possess a strong motivation for interdisciplinary research.

The Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, with its tradition spanning more than 600 years, is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With over 1,300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and serves as a training center for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Epidemiologist to design and conduct epidemiological research in pediatric populations, focusing on the determinants of child health, the development of common childhood diseases, particularly obesity, and the prevention and long-term outcomes of childhood obesity and metabolic diseases.
The research group "Childhood Obesity and Metabolic Research", led by Antje Körner, investigates the development, mechanisms and health consequences of childhood obesity. The translational approach combines experimental research, clinical studies and genetic approaches. Our international and interdisciplinary team is closely integrated with the research structures of the Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, Helmholtz Munich, and leading local as well as national research consortia, such as the Excellence cluster LeiCeM, the German Center for Child and Youth Health (DZKJ), and our large children's and adolescents' cohort LIFE Child.
We have large, well-characterized cohorts up and running with a longitudinal setting and across the entire age range: LIFE Child (n~6000), Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort (n~2500), and Leipzig Adipose Tissue Childhood cohort (n~700), with deep phenotyping allowing for combining clinical, epidemiological, lifestyle and functional omics and multi-omics data.
Key Responsibilities

- Design, plan, and conduct epidemiological research projects, including cohort and intervention studies.
- Develop study protocols and statistical analysis plans.
- Analyze and interpret complex population-based, clinical, and/or health-related datasets.
- Preparation of scientific manuscripts, reports, presentations, and grant applications.
- Ensure high standards of data quality, reproducibility, and compliance with ethical and data protection regulations.
- Present research findings at national and international conferences and scientific meetings.
- Provide methodological expertise and consultation to ongoing research projects; collaborate closely with clinicians, statisticians, bioinformaticians, and other researchers
- Supervision junior researchers or students.

Required Qualifications
Education: Candidates should have a Ph.D. and/or M.D. degree in: Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Medicine, Health Sciences or a related discipline.
Professional Experience

- Experience in the design and implementation of epidemiological studies, large cohort studies.
- Experience working with large-scale health, clinical, or population-based datasets.
- Strong understanding of epidemiological study designs and methodologies.
- Experience with observational and interventional research.
- Experience in data cleaning, validation, and quality assurance.
- Familiarity with evidence-based medicine and public health principles.
- Track record of scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals is desirable.
- Experience in interdisciplinary and collaborative research environments.
- Knowledge of research ethics and data protection requirements.
- Experience in grant writing is an advantage.
- Knowledge of causal inference methods (e.g., Target Trial Emulation, Mendelian Randomization) is desirable.

Statistical and Analytical Skills

- Proficiency in at least one statistical programming language such as: R, SAS, Stata, Python.
- Experience with general statistical methods:
- Regression modeling
- Longitudinal data analysis
- Missing data methods
- Sensitivity analyses
- Knowledge of modern analytical approaches, including machine learning methods, is an advantage.

Personal Competencies

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent organizational and project management abilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.
- Communication skills: English - excellent; German - very good

Candidates with one or more of the following areas of expertise are particularly encouraged to apply:

- Cohort studies
- Precision medicine and risk prediction modeling
- Multi-omics, biomarker, or biobank data integration
- Obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or metabolic health research

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications.

As part of a joint initiative organized by the Graduate School (integrated Research Training Group, iRTG) of the German Research Foundation (DFG)-funded Collaborative Research Center (CRC) 1774 “Cardio-Diabetes Crosstalk (CARDDIAB),” we are seeking, starting October 1, 2026, several

doctoral researchers (65% TV-L E13)

This is a three-year fixed-term training position in accordance with the German Act on Fixed-Term Academic Contracts (WissZeitVG, pursuant to Section §2(1)).

About the CRC 1774
The CRC 1774 investigates how key metabolic “promoter organs”-adipose tissue, bone marrow, the gut, and the liver-communicate with the cardiovascular system and thereby influence the progression from health through prediabetes and type 2 diabetes to cardiovascular diseases. By combining comprehensively characterized patient cohorts with state-of-the-art multi-omics technologies, innovative imaging techniques, and methods from data science and artificial intelligence, the project aims to decipher the mechanisms underlying cardiometabolic diseases and develop new approaches for precision medicine at the interface of diabetology and cardiology.

Doctoral students work on interdisciplinary research projects spanning basic, translational, and clinical research. The focus is on organ-to-organ communication, metabolic regulation, inflammatory processes, cellular energy metabolism, and cardiovascular complications of diabetes within a highly collaborative and international research environment. You hold a master’s degree, a diploma, or an equivalent university degree with excellent academic performance in a relevant field, such as the life sciences, medicine, molecular biology, biochemistry, molecular medicine, biomedicine, epidemiology, or related disciplines.

Previous research experience and a strong interest in interdisciplinary biomedical research are advantageous. Excellent written and spoken English skills are required.
Doctoral Projects:
Please indicate your preferred doctoral projects in your application. Information on all advertised projects, the participating project leaders, and the research and training program can be found on the CRC 1774 website.

Outstanding academic performance and a strong motivation for scientific work

Active participation in the structured training program and the scientific activities of the Integrated Graduate School
Willingness to engage in interdisciplinary collaboration and academic exchange within the CRC 1774
Timely production of scholarly publications and the doctoral dissertation
Compliance with the DFG guidelines for ensuring good scientific practice and the principles of responsible research

Worldline helps businesses of all shapes and sizes to accelerate their growth journey - quickly, simply, and securely. The Opportunity

We are looking for an Accountant to join our Group Accounting team in a role at the heart of our operations. You will work closely with operational teams, monitor key topics directly linked to business performance and development, and build strong relationships with PMOs and key partners across the organization.

Day-to-Day Responsibilities

Working closely with the Finance department and all financial functions of the Group (Order-to-Cash teams, Business Controllers, Consolidation, Finance Management, Treasury, etc.), you will be responsible for the following tasks:

- Perform daily accounting activities: bank operations, purchases, sales, payroll, VAT, and general accounting, including analytical coding of entries.
- Process financial transactions: verification, classification, calculation, accounting and data entry.
- Prepare supplier payment runs according to deadlines (twice per month).
- Monitor and reconcile customer and supplier accounts regularly.
- Work with the FBO teams to ensure timely customer billing.
- Participate in monthly, quarterly and annual closings under IFRS and local GAAP.

- Reconcile and justify open balance sheet items and participate in closing and balance sheet review meetings.
- Prepare and file statutory taxes: VAT, Corporate Income Tax, Environmental Taxes and other local taxes.
- Align monthly with the Consolidation team to validate intercompany positions (balance sheet and P&L) and prepare IFRS management reporting for consolidation purposes.
- Collaborate with Finance teams: Finance Business Operations, controlling, consolidation, treasury and other departments.
- Work with fiduciaries and consultants on local and international reporting.
- Manage relationships with external auditors and support internal and tax audits.
- Contribute to the design, maintenance and management of the internal control framework for existing and new activities.
- Continuously improve reporting processes and accounting controls.
- Ensure adherence to internal accounting policies.

Who Are We Looking For

We are seeking individuals capable of driving positive change—people who are proactive, passionate and ready to take initiative. In practice, this means:

- Minimum 3–4 years of experience in general accounting, either in a company or an audit firm.
- Autonomy in managing daily accounting tasks and standard tax declarations (especially VAT).
- Bachelor’s degree required.
- Strong rigor, analytical skills and the ability to structure complex topics.
- Ability to work independently while meeting strict deadlines.
- Capacity to translate business needs for internal stakeholders.
- Proficiency in English (an additional language is a plus).
- Willingness to learn more about accounting, tax and reporting.
- Solid command of Excel and SAP

What we offer

- Growth: The opportunity to progress in a fast-growing environment.
- Culture: Join a team that values proximity and entrepreneurial spirit.

Shape the evolution.

We are pushing towards the next frontiers of payments technology, and we look for big thinkers to join our journey. People with passion, can-do attitude and a hunger to learn and grow. Here you’ll work with ambitious colleagues from around the world, take on unique challenges as a team, and make a real impact on the society. Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon

The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range.

Institute of Material Systems Modeling

The Institute of Material Systems Modeling works on methods for virtual material and process development. Computational methods and artificial intelligence are used to optimize materials and their application from the atomic level to the system level.

PhD position in Agentic AI in Computational Modeling

JobID: 1061 - 2026/MS 7
Location: Geesthacht
Application deadline: 23 September, 2026

Developing computational models and running computer simulations in science and engineering still requires substantial expert knowledge. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) offers a great opportunity to automate these demanding tasks to a large extent. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a doctoral student in the area of agentic AI in computational modeling.

Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. The position is part-time (planned with 19.5 h/week).
Together with our team, you will push the frontier of agentic AI systems in computational modeling. That is, you will develop systems that leverage agentic AI to automate the development and execution of computer simulations. The objective is creating largely autonomous systems for computational modeling. The main application areas are the various areas of computational science and engineering with a strong focus on computational material science (both at the macroscale and atomic scale), biomedical engineering/biomechanics, and process engineering. However, also applications in environmental modeling (in particular coastal research and climate research) are potentially of interest.
You should have a master's degree in computational engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, or any other field closely related to computational modeling in science and engineering. You have a strong background in the theoretical foundations of engineering, science and applied mathematics. It is an advantage (though not mandatory) if you have prior knowledge in ontologies, knowledge graphs, and/or robotics.

You have demonstrated your excellent skills by outstanding grades during your bachelor's and master's program, in particular in those courses related to this call. You have very good programming skills in Python and ideally also C++. Proven experience in code development is crucial and will be checked during the job interview. Moreover, you have strong skills in communicating science in English.

• You independently plan, build, monitor, and optimize different campaign types within Search, continuously refining bidding strategies and account structure within established frameworks
• You create regular analyses and reports based on relevant KPIs, and translate your findings into clear, actionable recommendations for campaign steering
• You keep a close eye on campaign performance and proactively steer campaigns toward our defined goals
• You continuously scout for new trends, tools, and optimization potential in the SEA space, and reliably assess which are worth pursuing
• You help shape and refine processes around bidding strategies, automation, and campaign testing
• You run structured A/B tests to validate new approaches and identify incremental performance gains
• You take ownership of your own projects, from concept through execution, within the Text-Ads domain

ProfilYour profile - this is what we expect from you
• Successfully completed university degree in Economics, Business Administration, Marketing, or a related field
• You bring at least 3 years of professional experience in SEA/PPC, ideally including work with large keyword sets and performance-driven campaign management
• You are confident using relevant SEA tools such as Google Ads, Google Analytics, and Microsoft Advertising
• You have initial experience with Google Ads Scripts, or a strong motivation to learn and build automation skills
• You are comfortable using Generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude) to support ad copy creation and speed up campaign analysis
• You are a genuine team player with strong communication skills and enjoy technical exchange with your colleagues
• Your structured thinking and analytical skills help you spot potential and solve problems proactively and independently
• You are fluent in English (C1) and German language skills are a plus
